newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistani, Indian PMs to meet in Maldives in May.
newsitem.headline: Pakistani, Indian PMs to meet in Maldives in May.

text.p: The Indian and Pakistani prime ministers will meet in the Maldives in May on the sidelines of a South Asian summit conference there, a senior Pakistani official said on Monday.

Foreign Secretary Shahshad Ahmad told reporters at a conference on human development in South Asia the two prime ministers were certain to meet during the summit of the seven-nation South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation (SAARC) set for May 12-14.
"The two prime ministers will meet and substantive matters are likely to be discussed...including the core issue of Kashmir," he said.
"We have to go a long way, the issues involved are complex and deep rooted, but what is gratifying is that we have agreed to continue the talks," Ahmad said.

He was referring to his meeting last month with Indian foreign secretary Salman Haidar that marked a resumption of peace talks between the two nations after a three-year deadlock due to deep differences over the divided Himalayan region of Kashmir.
The two foreign secretaries -- the highest-ranking civil servants in their foreign ministries -- ended four days of upbeat talks on March 31 and agreed to meet again in Islamabad.
But they failed to set dates, partly because of the political turmoil in India where Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda faces a vote of confidence in parliament on April 11.
Pakistani Foreign Minister Gohar Ayub Khan and his Indian counterpart Inder Kumar Gujral are to meet in New Delhi this week after a Non-Aligned Movement ministerial meeting on April 7-8.
India and Pakistan have fought three wars since their independence from Britain in 1947, two of them over Kashmir.
